chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Sinan, said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: The testimony of the midwife is valid regarding the newborn, when it cries and shouts, concerning inheritance, and he inherits one-quarter of the inheritance by the measure of the testimony of one woman. I said, 'And if there were two women?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Their testimony is valid regarding half of the inheritance.'
ai.seo_question: How is inheritance determined for a newborn based on a midwife's testimony in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the evidentiary standards for a newborn's inheritance rights, establishing that a single midwife's testimony grants the child a quarter share, while two midwives' testimonies are required for a half share. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle of accepting female testimony in specific contexts of birth and lineage, ensuring the child's financial rights are secured immediately upon the 'first cry' (istihlal) even before full paternity is confirmed.
